10050081:
State of Maine STATE BOARD OF EDUCATION Testimony of Edmond Morin, Chair of the Career and Technical Education Committee
of The Maine State Board of Education Regarding LD 972: An Act to Change the Entity Responsible for Operating the Career And Technical Education Center in Machias to Regional School Unit 37
Sponsored by: Representative Strout Date: May 5, 2025
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and Honorable Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs:
My name is Edmond Morin, Career and Technical Education Chair for the Maine State Board of Education. In addition to facilitating the dispersal of federal Career and Technical Education money, the CTE Committee actively supports Career and Technical Education in Maine which is taught in 27 CTE Centers and Regions across the State. On behalf of the State Board of Education I am testifying Neither for Nor Against LD 972: An Act to Change the Entity Responsible for Operating the Career and Technical Education Center in Machias to Regional School Unit 37.
CTE programs have been offered at Machias High School for many years but most of the programs offered through Coastal Washington County Institute of Technology take place at a facility in Columbia. Online CWCIT is described as being part of MSAD 37. From what we understand several years ago MSAD 37 received a $2 Million dollar state grant to purchase and renovate a former supermarket in Columbia and began offering Career and Technical Education programs there. The building, which was considered to be centrally located, is owned by RSU 37 which pays expenses, including for teachers.
Administratively CTE Centers are associated with high schools under the overall leadership of that school's superintendent. A difficulty faced by the Coastal Washington County Institute of Technology stems from questions about financial control which is now in the hands of the Superintendent in Machias.
This has led to confusion and some rather unfortunate difficulties, having cost CWCIT state money to put an addition onto the building in Columbia and funds to pay for vans used to transport students to job sites especially health care students to clinicals.
The Maine State Board of Education greatly admires Maine's public school Superintendents and CTE Directors and has no desire to get in the middle of discussions about who should be the fiscal agent for CWCIT.

But one wonders if the way to go about selecting the fiscal agent for CWCIT should be done by legislation.
There are two places in Title 20-A which may be applicable in this situation. Section 405-I, among Powers and Duties of the State Board of Education, is to "act upon applications to alter the delivery of career and technical education within career and technical education regions and center areas." Section 8307-A sets forth reorganization procedures for CTE's including presenting a multi-element reorganization plan to the state board of education for its approval. Among the items in the plan are describing the deficiencies in the current method of providing career and technical education, presenting an alternative organizational method, presenting a method for assigning title to and obligations for property and indebtedness respectively of any region or center affected by a reorganization plan. The statute also provides for an assessment by the Commissioner and local voter approval.
So, the question posed by the State Board of Education is whether parties involved in this matter should proceed with this legislation or should they prepare a plan that can be submitted to the board. In which ever a way this is resolved we would like to see a structure that administers funds in the most efficient and logical manner for all programs that are offered with the hope of increasing that number with no loss of funding or opportunity for the students of coastal Washington County.
192368:
Lucille Willey, Director, Coastal Washington County Institute of Technology (CWCIT)
In support of LD 972 An Act to Change the Entity Responsible for Operating the Career and
Technical Education Center in Machias to Regional School Unit 37
Good morning. My name is Lucille Willey, and I am the Director of the Coastal Washington County Institute of Technology. Thank you for the opportunity to speak in support of LD 972.
CWCIT is a small Career and Technical Education Center in westem Washington County. In Maine, CTE schools are structured as either Centers or Regions. Regions are independent units governed by a
cooperative board. Centers, like ours, are governed by a single school administrative unit----typically where the programs are housed.
Our situation is unique. Although CWCIT is govemed by Machias, most of our programs, students, staff, and facilities are in RSU 3'7. In 2019, RSU 37, Machias, and partner districts wrote a grant to start 4 new
programs within CWCIT. The grant was awarded, and then the committee had to agree on a building to
house the new programs. RSU 37 purchased a building within its parameters and the 4 new programs started up in the fall of 2021 in the building purchased by RSU 27, in addition to the 2 that were already in existence in Machias and I existing program at Jonesport-Beals. Since then, the RSU 37 building has
been renovated to accommodate seven programs, with plans for more. Yet, the Center's governance remains with Machias.
This mismatch causes daily administrative complications. For example, RSU 37 hires and supervises
most of the staff, but Machias is listed as their employer in state systems. So, for staff certification or
payroll issues, RSU 37 must go through Machias---adding unnecessary steps.
We've lost significant opportunities because of this confusion. In 2022, we were automatically
disqualified fiom a $480,000 infrastructure grant because the RSU 37 superintendent----who oversees the actual building---signed the application, instead of the Machias superintendent. We also lost out on a
Perkins-funded van due to disagreements over ownership, insurance, and where it would be housed.
Simple decisions--like setting calendars, approving stipends, or clarifying student policies--require
approval from both RSU 37 and Machias, and sometimes even Machias town officials. It's inefficient
and delays progress.
LD 972 would resolve this by aligning CWCIT governance with where the majority of our operations occur---in RSU 37. Machias and Jonesport-Beals programs would become satellites. This change would
streamline operations, reduce confusion, and better serve our students.
CWCIT went through a Comprehensive School Review during the 23-24 school year. The final report
describes many of the complications that I have just talked about. Then it states "This unusual structure has created confusion within the CTE's operations and within the development of its schoolwide cultural
identity. It is recommended that a legislative change be considered that would assign CWCIT to RSU
37." And then under the recommendations, it is recommended by this committee, of which Dwight
Littlefield, State CTE Director, was a member, that we consider restructuring the governance of CWCIT
to reflect legislative intention, and work toward a legislative change that will reflect the current
operational structure.
Thank you for your time and your support for Career and Technical Education in Maine.
10054062:
LD972 An Act to Change the Entity Responsible for Operating the Career and Technical Education Center in Machias to Regional School Unit 37
My name is Lucille Willey. I am the Director of the Coastal Washington County Tech Center in Western Washington County. This bill proposes a vital administrative change that would significantly improve operations for our school.
Background and Current Situation
Prior to the fall of 2022, students from Washington Academy, Jonesport-Beals, Machias, and Narraguagus had very limited access to any type of career and technical education. Despite the fact that Machias was technically approved as a center, there was minimal movement between schools for the 4 available programs, with many students unable to participate at all.
In 2018, RSU 37 identified an opportunity through the Fund for Efficient Delivery of Educational Services (FEDES) to seek funding for creating more CTE options to students within the Western Washington County area. The SAD 37 superintendent invited all superintendents and board chairs to a meeting to discuss the FEDES grant opportunities. From that initial meeting, this group, along with other administrators, school board members, and citizens from the communities formed a group and met regularly for the purpose of planning a Down East Maine CTE Collaborative. In December of 2018, the group was notified that RSU 37 as the fiscal agent would be awarded $2,062,667 to meet the following goals:
1. To increase CTE programming options for students in CWCIT catchment area. 2. To provide new CTE programs at a location and time that would encourage students to enroll in programs of interest. 3. To ensure the sustainability of the 2019-20 four new programs at a satellite site. 4. To work toward implementation of the new CTE statutes that went into law with the passage of LD1843 for Title 20-A MRSA. 5. To offer programs that will prepare students for employment in current or emerging occupations. 6. To expand CTE to middle schools and students enrolled in alternative education.
The intent of this project was to have a site within RSU 37 to operate the four new programs. Once the group was told that the grant was approved, Machias School Department was unwilling to accept that the project would be housed in RSU 37 and then the State would not release the money until the location issue was resolved. The group agreed to hire Lyndon Kech from PDT architects to do a study of available buildings and locations within our catchment area. They narrowed the choices to 2. One was in Machias and the other in RSU 37. The one in RSU 37 was ranked number one, in part due to the fact that it would allow for additional programs over time. The one in Machias would not. Additionally the building in Machias was for sale for $750,000 and the one in RSU 37 was available at a much reduced rate ($150,000) because the owners were excited about it becoming a site for CTE. Machias disagreed with a decision to go

with the RSU site, and the project was at a standstill. And independent facilitator, Fern Desjardins, State School Board member, was hired as a facilitator. There were several public meetings and it was very clear that Machias was willing to lose the opportunity for all students if it was not going to be in Machias. After many heated discussions, many of the Machias residents and Board members started to speak up and the Machias school board then voted to allow the project to be in RSU 37.
In the years before 2018, that State had issued extra vocational subsidy for at least two years in a row. This was an initiative to put more emphasis on CTE. Early on in the planning process of the FEDES grant, the Machias superintendent mentioned they could hold the money so it could be used to help this project, but that never happened.
In the fall of 2020, the doors opened to the facility at 11 Addison Road, in Columbia, Maine with four programs. Jonesport-Beals had been working with CWCIT to start an Aquaculture program as a satellite at their school. That program also started in the fall of 2020.
This created a unique situation where the majority of the programs were now located in RSU 37, but the center was Machias, where only 2 programs were located within their high school. It was hard to know at that time how complicated that setup would be for operations. The center in other schools is located where the majority of programs, students, and staff are located, and programs in other areas are satellites of that Center. Over the period of the last 5 years, I have had the opportunity to see why that is the best scenario.
Remarkable Growth and Current Structure
In five years, CWCIT has expanded from 4 to 11 programs, with the majority housed in the RSU facility. This center, located in RSU 37, has actually become the operational hub for CTE in Western Washington County.
 It is the building where most students attend.  The whole CWCIT follows the RSU 37 calendar and storm delays  10 of the 14 total staff members work at the RSU facility  Students from all four sending schools attend daily
Administrative Challenges Under Current Structure
Despite the operational reality that RSU 37 serves as the center's main hub, Machias remains the designated fiscal agent, creating numerous challenges:
1. Logical Disconnect: First of all, it makes little sense for the Machias School Dept. and Town Council to hold operational controls over a CTE school that has most of it's programs in another school district.

2. Grant Application Issues: A $480,000 infrastructure grant application was automatically disqualified because it was signed by the RSU superintendent, despite RSU 37 being the district undertaking the renovation program. This was in no way due to Machias being unwilling to sign the application, it was simply a mistake on the part of both entities which could have been avoided if there was one fiscal agency to deal with.
3. Equipment Procurement Barriers: A planned purchase of a 9-passenger van for student transport to clinical sites was delayed due to different operating procedures between the two entities, Machias and RSU, and by the time we were able to complete the purchase, which had been approved by Perkins, the Machias finance officer emailed the new Perkins director and was told that the preference now had become not to use Perkins funding for vans which would hold 10 passengers, but for activity vans which would hold 15 and was about twice as much money. So the recommendation from both superintendents was not to use the money to buy the van. This was May and the funds had to be reallocated spent within about a month.
4. Staff Management Complications: Staff working at the RSU 37 building (10 of the 14 total) are considered Machias employees, even though they are hired and paid through RSU 37. This creates certification tracking issues, and other reporting issues by having
5. Financial Strain: RSU 37 fronts significant amounts of money for salaries, benefits, building costs, equipment maintenance, and so on before receiving the first quarterly subsidy payment from Machias which comes to them in November. RSU 37 also has about $1.5 million of its own funds invested in the building plus a $600,000 bond.
6. Purchases are complicated. We go through Machias for Perkins and through RSU 37 for all other items. This has caused delivery issues, since everything through Perkins has a Machias address, and everything through RSU 37 has our address. Also every vendor we purchase from, regardless of the funding we use, has to be listed as a vendor. Some are vendors of both entities, some are not, so that creates a timing issue while companies are being set up as vendors.
To be clear, both entities have tried to make this work for the past 5 years and neither entity has tried to do anything to make operations more difficult. But the more hands things have to go through, the more chance for error and the more chance that in the end, too much time has gone by to make opportunities happen, like the purchase of the van. Having one entity to work through would make everything smoother and more efficient.
And so, to summarize: Benefits and Fiscal Impact of Proposed Changes
1. Zero Cost to Taxpayers: Once again, there is no fiscal change to either entity. This change will not increase state spending, or require any additional resources.
2. Reduces Red Tape: By eliminating a duplication of efforts in administrative processes, we are putting more resources toward education rather than administration.

3. Supports Rural Communities: This CTE center is vital to Western Washington County's future, providing skills training that helps keep young people in our rural communities.
4. Promotes Accountability: Placing administrative responsibility with the district that houses the majority of the programs and creates very clear lines of accountability for program success.
The Career and Technical School established five years ago has made a tremendous difference for students throughout Western Washington County, offering pathways to high-wage careers without requiring a four-year degree. There is still room for expansion in the building in RSU 37 and there are plans in place to add Cosmetology, Plumbing, and Heating. By aligning administrative responsibility with operational reality, LD972 would ensure this valuable educational resource can continue to grow and serve students efficiently.
I urge the committee to vote to pass this bill. This legislative action represents a common-sense solution that aligns administrative responsibility with operational reality, creating efficiencies that will benefit students, working families, and taxpayers throughout all of Western Washington County.

"An Act to Change the Entity Responsible for Operating the Career and Technical Education Center in Machias to Regional School Unit 37" May 5, 2025
To: Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy and other Distinguished Members of the Education and Cultural Affairs Committee
From: Scott K. Porter, Superintendent of Schools, AOS 96 (11 Towns in the Machias Area) LD 972: "An Act to Change the Entity Responsible for Operating the Career and Technical Education Center in Machias to Regional School Unit 37"
I am writing in opposition to LD 972, "An Act to Change the Entity Responsible for Operating the Career and Technical Education Center in Machias to Regional School Unit 37". The Machias School Committee, which is the CTE governing body for Coastal Washington County Institute of Technology (CWCIT), is opposed to transferring all governing authority to RSU 37. The Machias School Committee is not opposed to RSU 37 being an additional CTE Center in law, having authority over their current satellite programs, as long as the students in the current CTE center configuration can attend all current programming and any new programs. The Maine Department of Education has pointed out there is a CTE Reorganization Statue (20A � M.R.S.A. 8307-A) that allows for the reorganization of a CTE center. I urge this Committee not to support LD 972.
Thank you.

Good Morning, Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy and distinguished members of the Education and Cultural Affairs
Committee. l am Representative Tiffany Strout from Harrington, representing the towns of Milbridge, Harrington,
Columbia, Columbia Falls, Centerville, Addison, Jonesport, Beals, Jonesboro, Roque Bluffs, Whitneyville and Machias in
beautiful Washington County and I am here today to present my bill LD 972 -- An Act to Change the Entity Responsible
for Operating the Career and Technical Education Center in Machias to Regional School Unit 37.
Like many, I wear several "hats" that come with different titles and responsibilities. Today l am here wearing several of those hats to share with you one of the best things that has come to my part of Washington County, probably in my
lifetime, the Coastal Washington County lnstitute of Technology (CWCIT).
I graduated from Narraguagus High School in MSAD #37 in 1997. When l was in school you basically had two career
paths, college and general. If you were signed up for the general course, you were looked upon as not going to make it very far in a career. The school offered automotive, technical drawing class and wood shop as extras. Unfortunately, there began a shift in what was seen as important and these programs closed at Narraguagus High School. However, MSAD#37 still invested in students' general education if they wanted to learn a trade. The students were lucky some in MSAD#37 had the insight to know trade schools would lead to a more successful careers and future.
From MSAD#37, students would travel to Machias High School for building trade classes and culinary studies. Students
would go to Ellsworth for automative, diesel, CDL and more. Students would also go to Bucksport for welding and Mount Desert Island for boat building. The MSAD#37 board had the financial investment of the community for students to attend
these schools. While students were traveling, finally, Machias, the current Governance head of the trade schools in Western Washington County, approved Narraguagus High School for Law Enforcement and the Nursing programs.
This format continued until there was an opportunity to receive a $2.1 million grant from the State of Maine to open a vocational school in Coastal Washington County. Everyone was so excited to have this great opportunity brought to the area, but we almost lost the grant due to a disagreement on where the facility should be located, similar to a school we did lose in the early 1990s because of the same issue. Eventually, it was decided the best opportunity for the future of the trade school was to invest in a building in Columbia, Maine which would be run by MSAD#37. Finally, CWCIT was able to be opened in the fall of 2020. With the award of the original grant, Aquaculture programs were able to be offered at
Jonespolt -- Beals High School.
When CWClT was first opened, the school was at capacity with 45 students for the programs that could be offered that first fall. Seeing that there was a lot of interest in these types of education programs, the board of MSAD#37 decided to invest in expanding the building and offering new programs. In looking at this, there was another opportunity for a
$450,000 infrastructure grant through the State of Maine. Here is where the confusion begins...

District ll Addison, Beals, Columbia, Columbia Falls, Harrington, Jonesboro, Jonesport, Machias, Milbridge, Roque Bluffs, Whitneyville, Centerville Township, and North Washington (Part)

After several meetings between the superintendents of Machias and MSAD#37, it was decided the superintendent of MSAD#37 would sign the papers since MSAD#37 would be overseeing the grant, distributing the funds and making any matching dollar needs. Unfortunately, that was the incorrect decision, and we lost the $450,000 grant.
Because MSAD#37 residents wanted to continue to invest in the trades, MSAD#37 board took out a $450,000 loan to help cover the cost of the renovations and expansions. Those cost have been well spent as there are now about 150
students enrolled in the programs.
in 5 short years MSAD# 37 has invested over $1 million to fund and grow the program offerings at the CWClT in
Columbia. Program offerings are automotive, diesel, welding, nursing, early childhood, law enforcement and CDL. Jonesport still has a growing aquaculture program and this year, computer technology was added to the building trade and culinary offerings in Machias.
CWClT is more than just a school. CWCIT is changing people's lives. There are students who were making some bad choices, but because they were able to take and pass their CDL test, they know they can be randomly drug tested and
could lose their license. Drugs are a major problem in our area. This school gives kids an opportunity for a start at a
good career out of high school as many may choose not to go on to college, even a community college.
The students who attend CWCIT travel from four surrounding schools, Washington Academy, Machias Memorial High School, Jonesport Beals High School and Narraguagus Jr/Sr High School. When they are on the sports field or on the
basketball court they are there to win for their sending schools. lt is the Raiders, Bulldogs, Royals and Knights, but at
CWClT they are all technical trade students working together on projects.
Nothing highlights this more than the nursing program. This year the students in the nursing program competed in the Nursing Knowledge Bowl and took the Gold award at Ski|lsUSAll Those four students were from Lubec, Machiasport, Jonesport and Harrington. The community is very proud of the students and are now helping them to raise funds to go to
Nationals.
So, why is there a need for this bill? This bill would replace Machias as the governing body with MSAD#37. That is it.
What this bill will do is specific to Western Washington County CWClT oversight. Because MSAD#37 has 7 of the 11 programs, it would make sense both logically and for efficiency to have the place with the most programs be the
governing body.
This bill will not change any structures in place, any students who can attend the schools and programs, any transportation or any payment reimbursement or requirements to be a trade school. The only change would be who receives the funding from the state for disbursement and bring clarity to who can sign and work on grants. This will bring efficiency and clarity for future growth of the school and programs. My hope is to be able to add more adult education
opportunities as well as programs for high school students.
More efficiency means more programs that can be offered. The more programs offered the more students can attend and the more our communities can grow and thrive.
As l started out with this testimony, l wear many hats. l am putting this bill fonrvard today as a Legislator, a MSAD# 37 school board member, a concerned citizen and most importantly a mom of a student who received his CDL and is
currently taking welding his senior year at CWClT, knows firsthand the difference this school is making in students' lives.
Thank you for your time today and I would be glad to answer any questions.
